title: Hybrid dequant stitcher + KV window tiler for improved INT8/FP8 attention throughput
author: Samira Khan
release_notes: Improves INT8/FP8 attention throughput by 18-26% depending on sequence length; reduces small-batch latency variance. No API changes.
description: Summary: Introduces a hybrid dequant stitcher that fuses per-layer dequant operations with attention kernels, and a KV window tiler that maintains aligned KV cache windows for tiled attention execution. Motivation: production workloads showed tail latency spikes and throughput cliffs when using per-layer dequant on mixed INT8/FP8 models with our continuous batcher. This PR reduces memory copies and enables vector-friendly kernel paths while keeping KV cache windowing compatible with rolling KV eviction. Design: (1) Dequant stitcher: rewrites the last dequant + scale ops into a tiled fused operator that emits FP16 fragments directly into attention microkernels. The stitcher uses a two-pass schedule: layer-local scalar folding followed by tile-level requantization hints for the microkernel. (2) KV window tiler: tracks active KV ranges per request and emits aligned tile boundaries so the attention kernels can read contiguous slices without per-token index arithmetic. (3) Scheduler integration: continuous-batcher and the request router were extended with a small compatibility matrix to route requests to the fused path only when model/sequence quantization profiles match (smoothquant-backed heuristics included). Backwards compatibility: non-matching models fall back to the existing dequant path. Performance: internal benchmarks (see bench/ci artifact) show 18-26% median throughput improvement for INT8-attention on T4/P4-like profiles and latency p95 reductions of 12-19% for small-batch PLG workloads. FP8 models see 10-15% throughput gains due to reduced copy overheads. Testing: added unit tests for stitcher IR rewrites, end-to-end perf tests in perf/bench_dequant_smoothquant.py, and stress tests for KV window eviction (long-seq, mixed-latency pattern). CI: all builds passed including perf harness; perf CI compares new baseline automatically. Rollout plan: staged rollout on Dedicated canaries (10% traffic) for 72h; collect cost/latency SLOs, then ramp to 50% and full. If regressions exceed 3% in unit-eval quality or 5% in p95 latency, automatic rollback is configured. Checklist: - [x] IR rewrite tests - [x] unit and integration tests - [x] perf harness runs - [x] docs: operator note in docs/ops/quant-ops.md - [x] Linear tickets linked: ENG-1429, ENG-1497

review_thread: Noah Green: Can you clarify how the stitcher handles per-head scale differences? || Samira Khan: The stitcher records per-head scale metadata and emits per-tile scale headers; the kernel consumes them with a cheap fused multiply—see runtime/kernels/attn_tiled_int8_kernel.cpp lines ~210-260. || Priya Menon: Are there any memory-pressure regressions on long-sequence workloads? || Samira Khan: We introduced a transient tile buffer that is bounded by tile_size*max_heads; measured memory usage increased by ~4% in worst case on 32K tokens but reduced overall copy churn. || Ethan Zhang: Please add an assertion for incompatible KV offsets to make debugging easier. || Samira Khan: Added an assert and a descriptive error message in kv_window_tiler.cc; pushed patch. || Priya Menon: Verified perf numbers on a P4 testbed, approve. || Noah Green: Approved after small comment fixes.
